title: Annual Population Survey: employment, inactivity and qualifications
quality: APS is a household survey; LA estimates rest on a few hundred respondents per LA (far fewer for 16-24 sub-groups). Nomis 95% CIs (`ci`, +/- percentage points) are typically +/-4-6 pts for 16-64 rates and +/-10-20 pts for youth rates or reasons for inactivity at LA level. LFS/APS is badged 'official statistics in development' after 2023-24 response-rate problems and reweighting.
limitations: Values Nomis does not publish (sample size 0-2 / disclosive, '!') and estimates Nomis flags unreliable (sample 3-9, CI withheld, '*') are null with suppressed=true (180 rows) and the Nomis status in attrs.status; for '*' rows the published figure is kept in attrs.unreliable_estimate for reference only. Temporary-sick and discouraged reasons are suppressed for all three LAs. Annual points are the same rolling 12-month window each year (Jul-Jun), not calendar years. Year-to-year LA changes are usually within sampling error. Qualifications use RQF levels from 2022 (not comparable with older NVQ series) and are only released for Jan-Dec windows, so qualification rows have a different period. Reasons for inactivity sum to ~100% of inactive 16-64. num/den are survey-weighted counts rounded to the nearest 100. APS excludes most communal establishments (e.g. many student halls).

title: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings: median pay by residence and workplace
next_update: Oct/Nov each year (provisional), revised the following year
quality: Accredited official statistics from a 1% sample of HMRC PAYE records (employer-reported). `ci` is an approximate 95% half-width derived from the Nomis coefficient of variation (attrs.cv_pct): 1.96 x CV x value.
limitations: Latest year is provisional and revised a year later. Employees only (no self-employed). Estimates with CV > 20% are suppressed by ONS (null, suppressed). Residence vs workplace gap indicates commuting to higher-paid jobs elsewhere (e.g. London). No BEDS total (medians cannot be summed).

title: Census 2021 small-area labour-market, skills, care and disability profile
quality: Accredited official statistics (Census 2021, ~97% person response, estimates adjusted for non-response). LA, region and England rows are the published LA-level figures; BEDS sums the three LA counts and recomputes %.
limitations: Census day 21 March 2021 fell in the third COVID-19 lockdown: furloughed people were counted as employed (temporarily away), labour-market activity may differ from normal, and students were counted at their term-time address (some were living elsewhere). Cell-key perturbation adds small noise to every cell, so LSOA counts do not sum exactly to LA totals and very small counts (<10) are unreliable; LSOA-to-LA sums differ slightly from LA rows. 2021 LSOAs differ from 2011 LSOAs (splits/merges), so direct comparison with 2011 needs the ONS LSOA11->LSOA21 lookup. Inactive/unemployed definitions use the ILO-style Census questions for the week before Census day; 'unemployed' includes full-time students seeking work. Hidden-potential pool = LT sick or disabled + looking after home/family + other (all 16+, incl. 65+).

title: Census 2021 origin-destination: residence vs place of work (LA)

title: 16-18 (key stage 5) attainment and retention by local authority
geography: LA, region, England, Bedfordshire (3 UAs, student counts only)
quality: Accredited official statistics covering state-funded schools and colleges; LA is the location of the institution, not student residence.
limitations: Average point scores cannot be summed or averaged to a Bedfordshire figure (no entry counts published), so Bedfordshire rows exist only for student counts. T level results are not published at LA level in this data set (national only) - a gap. Bedford's figures are dominated by Bedford College, which draws students from a wide area. 2020/21 TAGs and 2021/22 transitional grading are not comparable with later years. Retention data cover students in two-year programmes; England figures come from the national cohort time series. Small-cohort suppression (c/x/z) -> null.

quality: Official statistics from local authority Client Caseload Information System (CCIS) tracking of academic-age 16-17 residents; 'NEET' and 'not known' are averages of the Dec, Jan and Feb monthly snapshots (so LA counts can be fractional), participation is at end of December. title: Jobs density and total jobs
quality: Official statistics combining BRES, APS (self-employment), DWP and MoD data; rounded to nearest 1,000 jobs.
limitations: Jobs are counted at the workplace, people may hold more than one job. Self-employment component comes from APS and carries sampling error. Denominator is the mid-year estimate of 16-64 population.

indicators.label: Jobs density
indicators.description: Total jobs / resident population aged 16-64. <1 means fewer local jobs than working-age residents (net out-commuting). BEDS value computed here.

title: Subnational population projections, 2022-based (principal)
next_update: Unknown (SNPP normally every 2 years; next likely 2024-based)
quality: Official statistics (ONS); projections, not forecasts. They assume recent trends in births, deaths and migration continue and do not model local policy or development (e.g. housing growth or a resort opening).
limitations: Base year 2022; base pre-dates the mid-2023 to mid-2025 MYEs so early projection years will not match published estimates. Migration assumptions dominate at LA level and 18-24 counts are sensitive to student migration. No uncertainty intervals at LA level.

title: Education and training providers for 14-19 and adult skills (GIAS)
publisher: Department for Education - Get Information About Schools
quality: Administrative register maintained by DfE from establishments and LAs; status, type and address are reliable, but pupil numbers and % FSM are copied from the last school census (CensusDate attribute) and some fields are self-reported by establishments.
limitations: Open establishments in Bedford, Central Bedfordshire and Luton that are secondary, all-through, 16-19, UTC/studio, FE/sixth-form college, HEI, alternative provision (age 15+), special schools with post-16 (statutory high age >16) and independent schools with 16+ provision; plus FE and sixth-form colleges in neighbouring LAs within 25 km of the site. Middle schools (9-13, Bedford/Central Bedfordshire three-tier system) and primaries are excluded. Pupil numbers and % FSM are blank for FE colleges, HEIs and many independents (not collected via the school census) and FE college counts are a single head-office record - campuses are not separate rows, so the point is the registered address. GIAS no longer publishes Ofsted grades (ofsted_rating is null; use Ofsted management information). Independent training providers and employer apprenticeship providers are NOT included: no open download links UKPRN to delivery location. Distances are straight-line from the site (52.087N, 0.516W); OSGB36->WGS84 by Helmert (~2 m).

indicators.label: Pupils on roll (school census)
indicators.description: Number of pupils from the latest school census held in GIAS (NumberOfPupils); one point per provider with attrs (urn, type, phase, age range, sixth form, % FSM, LA, postcode, website, dist_km).

indicators.label: % pupils eligible for free school meals
indicators.description: PercentageFSM from GIAS (census-based) - deprivation marker for the provider's intake.

indicators.label: Number of open providers by category
indicators.description: Count of open providers in each Bedfordshire LA by category (breakdown).

title: Future 16-19 cohort: pupils by national curriculum year, FSM and SEN
quality: Accredited official statistics from the January school census (all schools including independent for year-group counts); full count, no sampling error.
limitations: Counts are by school location (LA where the school is), not pupil residence - Luton and Central Bedfordshire have material cross-border flows (Hertfordshire, Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire). Excludes home-educated and children missing education. FSM % and SEN % are state-funded secondary schools only; in Bedfordshire's three-tier areas middle schools are counted as secondary. The derived pipeline_aged16_* indicators are a simple cohort roll-forward with NO adjustment for migration, mortality, or movement into/out of independent schools - they indicate scale, not a forecast. Suppressed values (c/x/z/low) are null.

indicators.label: Pupils by national curriculum year (Y7-Y13)
indicators.description: Headcount of pupils in each NC year group, all school types, latest January census (breakdown = year group).

indicators.label: Pupils in Y7-Y11
indicators.description: Sum of NC years 7-11, all school types (history 2021/22 onwards).

indicators.label: Pupils in school sixth forms (Y12-Y13)
indicators.description: Sum of NC years 12-13 in schools (excludes FE/sixth-form colleges).

indicators.label: Derived: pupils reaching age 16 by academic year
indicators.description: DERIVED indicator. Cohort roll-forward of the 2025/26 census: pupils in NC year N are aged N+4 at the start of that year, so they are aged 16 at the start of academic year T when N = 12 - (T - 2025). E.g. today's Y6 is the cohort aged 16 in 2031/32. period/breakdown = target year (start of academic year). No migration/mortality adjustment.

indicators.label: Derived: 16-18 cohort size by academic year
indicators.description: DERIVED indicator. Sum of the three single-year cohorts aged 16, 17 and 18 at the start of target academic year T (the 16-19 study cohort), rolled forward from the latest census as for pipeline_aged16_by_year. Only years whose three cohorts are all still in Y1-Y11 today (full school coverage) are given - earlier years would rely on school-only Y12-13 counts that omit FE colleges. No migration/mortality adjustment.

indicators.label: % eligible for FSM (state-funded secondary)
indicators.description: Percentage of pupils in state-funded secondary schools known to be eligible for free school meals (January census).

indicators.label: % with SEN support (state-funded secondary)
indicators.description: Percentage of pupils on SEN support (no EHC plan) in state-funded secondary schools - indicates support needs in the future cohort.

indicators.label: % with an EHC plan (state-funded secondary)
indicators.description: Percentage of pupils with an education, health and care plan in state-funded secondary schools.
